scope: Full independent recompute of all 20 frozen heldout records, source-K4/mosaic packing, PWP recurrence, and hardware admission attacks

pwp_recurrence_audit.reason_resources_not_matched: M150 candidate bundles a 1024-bit PWP source and ideal four-destination issue/write capability against the M143 B4 reference; storage, ports, area, energy and frequency are not matched.

findings.title: Same source does not imply one reusable 96-lane vector across destination blocks
findings.evidence: Across all four frozen INT8 operators, 774144 pairs of destination-block vectors from the same weight row were compared and zero pairs were identical. One destination vector is 768 bits; four destination blocks require four distinct 768-bit vectors or access to the full 6144-bit source weight row.
findings.impact: The architecture statement source_vectors_required_per_descriptor=1 with a 768-bit payload cannot produce four distinct destination-block contributions. The core hardware simplification behind source stationarity is therefore unsupported.
findings.required_action: Redefine the resident object as a 6144-bit full source row with explicit four-block extraction, or provide four independently banked 768-bit vectors and price all read ports, muxing, capacity and energy.

findings.title: Key-switch and load-to-use latency are absent
findings.evidence: There are 23522595 active row/source keys, but the recurrence charges descriptors and frozen weight tokens without an explicit source-key switch or store access latency. A one-cycle-per-active-key sensitivity increases the schedule to 96762797 cycles and reduces the ratio to 1.399929x.
findings.impact: 75.03M cycles is an optimistic lower bound whose dominant source-stationary control transition is unpriced.
findings.required_action: Implement a key-addressed executable scheduler/store interface and replay measured load-to-use and key-switch latency; do not treat the sensitivity value as a measurement.

findings.title: Four destination updates and accumulator write ports are assumed, not implemented
findings.evidence: 47034985 of 47040777 descriptors are full4 (99.987687%). M149 assumes four contribution vectors are preavailable and explicitly excludes accumulator commit and SRAM ports. Independent sensitivities yield 119968634 cycles with two writes and 213772648 with one write.
findings.impact: The 1.805x opportunity depends almost universally on four-way bandwidth. A two-port design falls to 1.129x; a one-port design is slower than M143.
findings.required_action: Provide integrated four-vector supply, four conflict-safe accumulator update ports, banking proof, VCS numeric replay, DC and macro-aware timing.

findings.title: Resident source store is undefined and unpriced
findings.evidence: A full source weight row is 6144 bits; the minimum full-row store for the current 16-source partition is 98304 bits and a whole operator is 42467328 bits. M150 explicitly has no resident store or macro evidence.
findings.impact: The vector reuse/feed premise has no capacity, banking, address, bandwidth, area or energy realization.
findings.required_action: Freeze a residency scope, replacement policy, bank mapping and macro interface, then include fill/refill traffic and energy in the recurrence.

findings.title: Signed negate mapping is materially exercised but not replayed
findings.evidence: The full recompute finds 17557357 negative events and 4389684 negative descriptors, both 9.33165% of their totals. M149 contains a standalone 9-bit-safe negate primitive, but M150 has no ordered descriptor-to-tuple_negate numeric replay.
findings.impact: Support-only counts do not prove that source transposition preserves signed residual arithmetic and destination ownership.
findings.required_action: Materialize ordered descriptors with signs and destinations, replay against the integer oracle, and integrate the M149 negate path with the actual vector source.

findings.title: The 1.805x ratio bundles unequal resource axes
findings.evidence: The M143 reference uses the B4/PWP512 path, while M150 combines source-K4, PWP1024 and ideal four-destination updates. The recurrence arithmetic is identical, but storage width, ports, area, bandwidth, energy and frequency are not matched.
findings.impact: The ratio cannot be attributed to source stationarity or cited as a hardware speedup.
findings.required_action: Report an axis-by-axis ablation and a matched-area/matched-bandwidth baseline.

findings.title: Source-K4 has no modeled cycle advantage over unrestricted M147 mosaic
findings.evidence: Source-K4 adds 3566 descriptors and 3196 cycles; its ratio versus M147 is 0.9999574. Only 362 of 25920000 rows differ.
findings.impact: The new ordering is a possible implementation simplification, not a performance result. With H01 unresolved, even that simplification is unproven.
findings.required_action: Sell only a verified supply/packer simplification after RTL; do not count M147's opportunity again as M150 speedup.

validated_strengths: All 20 heldout records and every requested aggregate were independently recomputed from frozen packed support and INT8 weights.
The source-K4 definition, all-zero producer floor, numeric-center tie ordering and unrestricted-mosaic bound are internally consistent.
The frozen four-bank recurrence and fair fixed8 service baseline reproduce exactly.
The production result already labels four-destination RTL, resident store, signed replay, macro, physical and headline claims as false.
review_disposition: Retain M150 only as a heldout opportunity/ordering probe. Reject 1.805357580618x as hardware performance. The first required milestone is a vector-supply and resident-store contract that resolves H01, followed by executable signed descriptors and four-port accumulator integration.
